statement: The Neanderthal and Denisovan lineages are estimated to have diverged from each other approximately 381,000-473,000 years ago — a distinct, more recent split than either lineage’s divergence from Homo sapiens (~550,000-765,000 years ago). A 2020 study additionally proposes the joint Neanderthal-Denisovan ancestral population itself interbred with a more distantly related "super-archaic" population (roughly 2 million years divergent) around 700,000 years ago, adding a layer of admixture complexity beneath the clean divergence figure without changing it.

sources.citation: Prüfer, K. et al. "The complete genome sequence of a Neanderthal from the Altai Mountains." Nature 505: 43-49.
sources.author: Prüfer et al.

sources.citation: Rogers, A.R., Harris, N.S., Achenbach, A.A. "Neanderthal-Denisovan ancestors interbred with a distantly related hominin." Science Advances 6(8): eaay5483.
sources.author: Rogers et al.

does_not_demonstrate: a "clean" two-population divergence uncomplicated by further admixture — see the Rogers et al. 2020 "super-archaic" admixture proposal noted in the statement
